date_note: The Record's article of 25 November gives no earlier day for FIFA's confirmation; it says the group claimed the attack 'last week'.
exec: FIFA says hackers accessed a limited set of personal and business information, a reminder that sports bodies are targets too.
plain: FIFA says hackers got into a limited set of personal and business information. A hacking group says it was behind it and has published data; FIFA says it is working with law enforcement.
summary: FIFA told The Record that hackers gained unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information, and that it is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement. The Record reports a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claimed the attack and published stolen data on a cybercriminal forum; those claims are unverified. FIFA did not respond to follow-up questions.
title: FIFA says hackers accessed a 'limited set of personal and business information'

validation.note: Single publisher (The Record) quoting FIFA's statement; the hacking group's claims are not verified. Not corroborated by a second outlet.

review.note: Compared FIFA statement, unverified group claim and no response to follow-ups against The Record
